sections.title: Grammar in plain English
sections.kick: Each sentence above already has a word-by-word breakdown.
items: 我累了 Wǒ lèi le means you have gotten tired. 了 marks a new situation. It does not mean English “have”. 我很累 Wǒ hěn lèi means “I'm tired”, and an adjective takes no 是. 我有点累 Wǒ yǒu diǎn lèi means “I'm a little tired”. 有点 is one chunk. yǒu can sound a bit like English “you”. It is 有, not 你.
我是累 is on a card above so it can be avoided. Save 是 for identity and categories. For adjectives, use 很, or 了 when the state is new.

的 de, neutral, links a description to a noun (棕色的鞋, 新的鞋子) and marks possession (我的, 你的). A short phrase can drop it: 新鞋. A longer description usually keeps it. There is no rule that every adjective must have 的.
也, 吗, and word order

也 yě means also or too and stands before the verb. 吗 ma makes a yes/no question and stands at the end. 你也喜欢吗 asks “Do you like them too?” The object can be left out. 你也喜欢！ states “You like them too!” That is the message that was sent. 我也喜欢你 means “I like you too”, because 你 follows 喜欢 and is the object. The chat sent 你也喜欢, and the object sentence was added on this page for comparison.
喜不喜欢, said in two messages

喜不喜欢 xǐ bu xǐhuan puts “like or not” inside the sentence: whether someone likes something. It does not use 吗. 不 stays bù before 喜, which is 3rd tone. 不 becomes bú only before a 4th tone. The question arrived as two messages: 你怎么知道我喜不喜欢 and then 你的新鞋. Together: How do you know whether I like your new shoes?
没有, 就, 会, 晃

没有 méiyǒu means “don't have”. Negate 有 with 没. 就 jiù means then, or as soon as. 会 huì means will, or tends to. 晃 huàng, 4th tone, means wag or sway. 见到你就会晃的尾巴 is a fragment on 我有尾巴: a tail that wags when I see you.

你真棒 Nǐ zhēn bàng is “You're awesome” or “You did great”. 真 is really. 棒 is great. 牛 niú alone is casual slang for impressive. 牛逼 niúbī is casual and vulgar: “fucking awesome” or “badass”. In that slang word, 逼 is a written stand-in for 屄. Ordinary 逼 means “to force” or “to compel”. Prefer 你真棒 or 牛 when you want the clean wording.
What was left off the page

The list sentence is anonymized wording. A personal name was replaced with 我 and with 你. An English joke in the chat used a wingman and a screenshot. The personal wording is not stored here. No photos and no contact details are on this page. The playful lines are language study.
How the tone marks are chosen

Dictionary tones are the pinyin with tone marks. Where several 3rd tones sit together, this page raises every 3rd except the last. The last 3rd stays low when another tone follows, and it can dip at a pause. 喜欢 is xǐhuan, with 欢 neutral. A speaker may group the words another way. Copy the marks, then trust your ear.
